sanskrit: nārada uvāca dṛṣṭo me puruṣaḥ śrīmān viśvarūpadharo 'vyayaḥ sarve hi lokās tatrasthās tathā devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ adyāpi cainaṃ paśyāmi yuvāṃ paśyan sanātanau
english: Nārada said: I have beheld the glorious, imperishable Person who bears the form of the universe. All the worlds abide within Him, and the gods together with the seers. Even now I see Him, as I gaze upon you two, O eternal ones.

sanskrit: yair lakṣaṇair upetaḥ sa harir avyaktarūpadhṛk tair lakṣaṇair upetau hi vyaktarūpadharau yuvām
english: With the very marks that Hari bears, He who wears an unmanifest form, with those same marks are you two endowed, who wear a manifest form.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭau mayā yuvāṃ tatra tasya devasya pārśvataḥ iha caivāgato 'smy adya visṛṣṭaḥ paramātmanā
english: There I beheld you two at the side of that God, and now this very day I have come here, sent forth by the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: ko hi nāma bhavet tasya tejasā yaśasā śriyā sadṛśas triṣu lokeṣu ṛte dharmātmajau yuvām
english: For who indeed could be His equal in splendor, in glory, in majesty, throughout the three worlds, save you two, the sons of Dharma?

sanskrit: tena me kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ nāma kṣetrajñasaṃjñitam prādurbhāvāś ca kathitā bhaviṣyanti hi ye yathā
english: By Him was disclosed to me before His name, which is called the Knower of the Field; and the manifestations were told to me, how and which shall come to be.

sanskrit: tatra ye puruṣāḥ śvetāḥ pañcendriyavivarjitāḥ pratibuddhāś ca te sarve bhaktāś ca puruṣottamam
english: There the men who are white, free from the five senses, are all of them awakened and devoted to the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: te 'rcayanti sadā devaṃ taiḥ sārdhaṃ ramate ca saḥ priyabhakto hi bhagavān paramātmā dvijapriyaḥ
english: They forever worship the God, and with them He takes delight; for the Lord, the Supreme Self, loves His devotees and is dear to the twice-born.

sanskrit: ramate so 'rcyamāno hi sadā bhāgavatapriyaḥ viśvabhuk sarvago devo bāndhavo bhaktavatsalaḥ sa kartā kāraṇaṃ caiva kāryaṃ cātibaladyutiḥ
english: He delights when worshiped, ever loving of His votaries—the All-devourer, the all-pervading God, the kinsman, tender to the faithful; He of surpassing might and radiance is the doer, the cause, and the effect alike.

sanskrit: tapasā yojya so ''tmānaṃ śvetadvīpāt paraṃ hi yat teja ity abhivikhyātaṃ svayaṃbhāsāvabhāsitam
english: Joining Himself to Him through austerity, He attains that which lies beyond Śvetadvīpa, that which is renowned as the splendor, illumined by its own self-shining radiance.

sanskrit: śāntiḥ sā triṣu lokeṣu siddhānāṃ bhāvitātmanām etayā śubhayā buddhyā naiṣṭhikaṃ vratam āsthitaḥ
english: That is the peace, throughout the three worlds, of the perfected ones whose selves are made pure; with this auspicious understanding He has undertaken the steadfast vow.

sanskrit: na tatra sūryas tapati na somo 'bhivirājate na vāyur vāti deveśe tapaś carati duścaram
english: There the sun gives no heat, nor does the moon shine forth, nor does the wind blow, while in the Lord of gods austerity hard to perform is practiced.

sanskrit: vedīm aṣṭatalotsedhāṃ bhūmāv āsthāya viśvabhuk ekapādasthito deva ūrdhvabāhur udaṅmukhaḥ sāṅgān āvartayan vedāṃs tapas tepe suduścaram
english: Mounting upon an altar of eight palms' height set upon the ground, the All-devouring God, standing upon one foot, with arms upraised and face turned northward, reciting the Vedas together with their auxiliary lore, performed austerity most hard to bear.

sanskrit: yad brahmā ṛṣayaś caiva svayaṃ paśupatiś ca yat śeṣāś ca vibudhaśreṣṭhā daityadānavarākṣasāḥ
english: That which Brahmā and the seers, and the Lord of creatures himself, and all the rest, the foremost of the wise, the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas—

sanskrit: nāgāḥ suparṇā gandharvāḥ siddhā rājarṣayaś ca ye havyaṃ kavyaṃ ca satataṃ vidhipūrvaṃ prayuñjate kṛtsnaṃ tat tasya devasya caraṇāv upatiṣṭhati
english: the Nāgas, the Suparṇas, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and the royal seers, all of the oblation to the gods and to the fathers that they ceaselessly offer according to rule—the whole of it draws near to the feet of that God.

sanskrit: yāḥ kriyāḥ saṃprayuktās tu ekāntagatabuddhibhiḥ tāḥ sarvāḥ śirasā devaḥ pratigṛhṇāti vai svayam
english: And those rites that are duly performed by men whose minds are bent on Him alone—all of these the God Himself receives upon His head.

sanskrit: na tasyānyaḥ priyataraḥ pratibuddhair mahātmabhiḥ vidyate triṣu lokeṣu tato 'smy aikāntikaṃ gataḥ iha caivāgatas tena visṛṣṭaḥ paramātmanā
english: None dearer to Him than the awakened great souls is found throughout the three worlds; therefore have I gone to single-minded devotion, and have come here, sent forth by Him, the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: evaṃ me bhagavān devaḥ svayam ākhyātavān hariḥ āsiṣye tatparo bhūtvā yuvābhyāṃ saha nityaśaḥ
english: Thus did the blessed God Hari Himself declare to me; intent on Him, I shall dwell forever together with you two.

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇāv ūcatuḥ dhanyo 'sy anugṛhīto 'si yat te dṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ na hi taṃ dṛṣṭavān kaś cit padmayonir api svayam
english: Nara and Nārāyaṇa said: Blessed are you, and graced, in that the Lord Himself was beheld by you; for none has ever seen Him, not even the lotus-born one himself.

sanskrit: avyaktayonir bhagavān durdarśaḥ puruṣottamaḥ nāradaitad dhi te satyaṃ vacanaṃ samudāhṛtam
english: Of unmanifest origin is the blessed Supreme Person, hard to behold; O Nārada, true indeed is the word you have spoken.

sanskrit: nāsya bhaktaiḥ priyataro loke kaś cana vidyate tataḥ svayaṃ darśitavān svam ātmānaṃ dvijottama
english: None in the world is found dearer to Him than His devotees; therefore He revealed His own Self to you, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tapo hi tapyatas tasya yat sthānaṃ paramātmanaḥ na tat saṃprāpnute kaś cid ṛte hy āvāṃ dvijottama
english: That station of the Supreme Self who is performing austerity, none attains it, save we two alone, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: yā hi sūryasahasrasya samastasya bhaved dyutiḥ sthānasya sā bhavet tasya svayaṃ tena virājatā
english: Whatever the radiance of a thousand suns gathered together might be, such is the radiance of that station, shining of its own accord through Him.

sanskrit: tasmād uttiṣṭhate vipra devād viśvabhuvaḥ pateḥ kṣamā kṣamāvatāṃ śreṣṭha yayā bhūmis tu yujyate
english: From that God, the All-pervading Lord, O brāhmaṇa, arises forbearance—O foremost of the forbearing—wherewith the earth is endowed.

sanskrit: tasmāc cottiṣṭhate devāt sarvabhūtahito rasaḥ āpo yena hi yujyante dravatvaṃ prāpnuvanti ca
english: And from that God arises savor, the benefactor of all beings, wherewith the waters are endowed and attain their fluidity.

sanskrit: tasmād eva samudbhūtaṃ tejo rūpaguṇātmakam yena sma yujyate sūryas tato lokān virājate
english: From Him alone has arisen the brilliance whose essence is the quality of form, wherewith the sun is endowed, and thereby illumines the worlds.

sanskrit: tasmād devāt samudbhūtaḥ sparśas tu puruṣottamāt yena sma yujyate vāyus tato lokān vivāty asau
english: From that God, the Supreme Person, has arisen touch, wherewith the wind is endowed, and thereby blows through the worlds.

sanskrit: tasmāc cottiṣṭhate śabdaḥ sarvalokeśvarāt prabhoḥ ākāśaṃ yujyate yena tatas tiṣṭhaty asaṃvṛtam
english: And from that Lord, the Master of all worlds, arises sound, wherewith space is endowed, and thereby it stands unbounded.

sanskrit: tasmāc cottiṣṭhate devāt sarvabhūtagataṃ manaḥ candramā yena saṃyuktaḥ prakāśaguṇadhāraṇaḥ
english: And from that God arises mind, which pervades all beings, wherewith the moon is joined, the bearer of the quality of light.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhūtotpādakaṃ nāma tat sthānaṃ vedasaṃjñitam vidyāsahāyo yatrāste bhagavān havyakavyabhuk
english: That station, named the generator of the six elements, is called the Veda, wherein the blessed Lord abides, companioned by knowledge, the enjoyer of oblations to gods and fathers.

sanskrit: ye hi niṣkalmaṣā loke puṇyapāpavivarjitāḥ teṣāṃ vai kṣemam adhvānaṃ gacchatāṃ dvijasattama sarvalokatamohantā ādityo dvāram ucyate
english: For those in the world who are stainless, free of merit and demerit, as they travel the path of safety, O best of the twice-born, the sun, dispeller of the darkness of all worlds, is said to be the gate.

sanskrit: ādityadagdhasarvāṅgā adṛśyāḥ kena cit kva cit paramāṇubhūtā bhūtvā tu taṃ devaṃ praviśanty uta
english: With all their limbs consumed by the sun, unseen by anyone anywhere, having become atoms, they then enter into that God.

sanskrit: tasmād api vinirmuktā aniruddhatanau sthitāḥ manobhūtās tato bhūyaḥ pradyumnaṃ praviśanty uta
english: Released even from Him, abiding in the body of Aniruddha, become as mind, they then further enter into Pradyumna.

sanskrit: pradyumnāc cāpi nirmuktā jīvaṃ saṃkarṣaṇaṃ tathā viśanti viprapravarāḥ sāṃkhyā bhāgavataiḥ saha
english: Released also from Pradyumna, the foremost of brāhmaṇas, the followers of Sāṃkhya together with the votaries of the Lord, enter then into Saṃkarṣaṇa, who is the living soul.

sanskrit: tatas traiguṇyahīnās te paramātmānam añjasā praviśanti dvijaśreṣṭha kṣetrajñaṃ nirguṇātmakam sarvāvāsaṃ vāsudevaṃ kṣetrajñaṃ viddhi tattvataḥ
english: Then, freed of the three qualities, they enter straightway into the Supreme Self, O best of the twice-born, the Knower of the Field, whose nature is without quality; know in truth that Vāsudeva, the dwelling-place of all, is the Knower of the Field.

sanskrit: samāhitamanaskāś ca niyatāḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ ekāntabhāvopagatā vāsudevaṃ viśanti te
english: With minds composed, restrained, their senses curbed, attained to single-minded devotion, they enter into Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: āvām api ca dharmasya gṛhe jātau dvijottama ramyāṃ viśālām āśritya tapa ugraṃ samāsthitau
english: We two also were born in the house of Dharma, O best of the twice-born, and, resorting to the lovely and broad Viśālā, have undertaken fierce austerity.

sanskrit: ye tu tasyaiva devasya prādurbhāvāḥ surapriyāḥ bhaviṣyanti trilokasthās teṣāṃ svastīty ato dvija
english: And those manifestations of that very God, dear to the gods, which shall arise abiding within the three worlds—to them be welfare, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: vidhinā svena yuktābhyāṃ yathāpūrvaṃ dvijottama āsthitābhyāṃ sarvakṛcchraṃ vrataṃ samyak tad uttamam
english: By us two, joined to our own ordinance as of old, O best of the twice-born, the all-difficult vow has been duly upheld, that highest of vows.

sanskrit: āvābhyām api dṛṣṭas tvaṃ śvetadvīpe tapodhana samāgato bhagavatā saṃjalpaṃ kṛtavān yathā
english: By us two also were you seen in Śvetadvīpa, O treasury of austerity, when, having come together with the Lord, you held converse with Him.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ hi nau saṃviditaṃ trailokye sacarācare yad bhaviṣyati vṛttaṃ vā vartate vā śubhāśubham
english: For all is fully known to us two, throughout the three worlds with their moving and unmoving things, whatever good or evil shall come to pass, or has passed, or now passes.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tayor vākyaṃ tapasy ugre 'bhyavartata nāradaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this speech of theirs, Nārada gave himself to fierce austerity, and, with palms joined, became wholly devoted to Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: jajāpa vidhivan mantrān nārāyaṇagatān bahūn divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi naranārāyaṇāśrame
english: He muttered duly many sacred formulas turned toward Nārāyaṇa for a celestial thousand years in the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: avasat sa mahātejā nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ tam evābhyarcayan devaṃ naranārāyaṇau ca tau
english: There dwelt that mighty-splendored, blessed seer Nārada, worshiping that very God, and those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kasya cit tv atha kālasya nāradaḥ parameṣṭhijaḥ daivaṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ pitryaṃ cakre tataḥ param
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, after some time, Nārada, born of the Lord Supreme, having performed the rite to the gods according to ordinance, performed thereafter the rite to the fathers.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ vacanaṃ prāha jyeṣṭho dharmātmajaḥ prabhuḥ ka ijyate dvijaśreṣṭha daive pitrye ca kalpite
english: Then the elder one, the lordly son of Dharma, spoke this word: Who is worshiped, O best of the twice-born, when the rite to the gods and the rite to the fathers are ordained?

sanskrit: tvayā matimatāṃ śreṣṭha tan me śaṃsa yathāgamam kim etat kriyate karma phalaṃ cāsya kim iṣyate
english: O foremost of the wise, declare this to me as it is handed down: why is this rite performed, and what fruit of it is sought?

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tvayaitat kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ daivaṃ kartavyam ity api daivataṃ ca paro yajñaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ
english: Nārada said: By you it was told before that the rite to the gods is to be done; and the deity, the highest sacrifice, is the eternal Supreme Self.

sanskrit: tatas tadbhāvito nityaṃ yaje vaikuṇṭham avyayam tasmāc ca prasṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ
english: Therefore, ever absorbed in Him, I worship the imperishable Vaikuṇṭha; and from Him there issued of old Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds.

sanskrit: mama vai pitaraṃ prītaḥ parameṣṭhy apy ajījanat ahaṃ saṃkalpajas tasya putraḥ prathamakalpitaḥ
english: It was indeed my father whom the gracious Supreme One begot; and I am that one's son, born of his will, fashioned first of all.

sanskrit: yajāmy ahaṃ pitṝn sādho nārāyaṇavidhau kṛte evaṃ sa eva bhagavān pitā mātā pitāmahaḥ ijyate pitṛyajñeṣu mayā nityaṃ jagatpatiḥ
english: I worship the fathers, O virtuous one, once the ordinance of Nārāyaṇa is fulfilled; thus that very blessed Lord, father, mother, and grandsire, the Master of the world, is forever worshiped by me in the sacrifices to the fathers.

sanskrit: śrutiś cāpy aparā deva putrān hi pitaro 'yajan vedaśrutiḥ praṇaṣṭā ca punar adhyāpitā sutaiḥ tatas te mantradāḥ putrāḥ pitṛtvam upapedire
english: And there is yet another sacred tradition, O god: the fathers worshiped their sons. The Vedic lore, once lost, was again taught by the sons; therefore those sons who gave the sacred formulas attained the rank of fathers.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ puraitad viditaṃ yuvayor bhāvitātmanoḥ putrāś ca pitaraś caiva parasparam apūjayan
english: Surely this was known of old to you two of purified souls: the sons and the fathers worshiped one another.

sanskrit: trīn piṇḍān nyasya vai pṛthvyāṃ pūrvaṃ dattvā kuśān iti kathaṃ tu piṇḍasaṃjñāṃ te pitaro lebhire purā
english: "Having first strewn the kuśa grass, then set down three rice-balls upon the earth"—but how did those fathers of old come to bear the name of the rice-ball?

sanskrit: naranārāyaṇāv ūcatuḥ imāṃ hi dharaṇīṃ pūrvaṃ naṣṭāṃ sāgaramekhalām govinda ujjahārāśu vārāhaṃ rūpam āśritaḥ
english: Nara and Nārāyaṇa said: This earth, girdled by the sea, once lost, Govinda swiftly raised up, having assumed the form of a boar.

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā tu dharaṇīṃ sve sthāne puruṣottamaḥ jalakardamaliptāṅgo lokakāryārtham udyataḥ
english: And having set the earth in its own place, the Supreme Person, His limbs smeared with water and mire, rose up for the sake of the world's work.

sanskrit: prāpte cāhnikakāle sa madhyaṃdinagate ravau daṃṣṭrāvilagnān mṛtpiṇḍān vidhūya sahasā prabhuḥ sthāpayām āsa vai pṛthvyāṃ kuśān āstīrya nārada
english: And when the time for the daily rite had come, the sun having reached the midpoint of the day, the Lord, swiftly shaking off the clods of earth clinging to His tusk, set them down upon the ground, having spread out kuśa grass, O Nārada.

sanskrit: sa teṣv ātmānam uddiśya pitryaṃ cakre yathāvidhi saṃkalpayitvā trīn piṇḍān svenaiva vidhinā prabhuḥ
english: Designating Himself in them, the Lord performed the rite to the fathers as prescribed, having consecrated three rice-balls by His own ordinance.

sanskrit: ātmagātroṣmasaṃbhūtaiḥ snehagarbhais tilair api prokṣyāpavargaṃ deveśaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ kṛtavān svayam
english: With sesame seeds born of the warmth of His own body and laden with their oil, the Lord of gods, facing eastward, Himself sprinkled them and brought the rite to its close.

sanskrit: maryādāsthāpanārthaṃ ca tato vacanam uktavān ahaṃ hi pitaraḥ sraṣṭum udyato lokakṛt svayam
english: And to establish the bounds of right usage He then spoke this word: I, the maker of the world, am Myself set upon creating the fathers.

sanskrit: tasya cintayataḥ sadyaḥ pitṛkāryavidhiṃ param daṃṣṭrābhyāṃ pravinirdhūtā mamaite dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āśritā dharaṇīṃ piṇḍās tasmāt pitara eva te
english: As He pondered at once the supreme ordinance of the rite to the fathers, "These clods of mine, shaken from My tusks, have come to rest upon the earth in the southern quarter; therefore these are indeed the fathers."

sanskrit: trayo mūrtivihīnā vai piṇḍamūrtidharās tv ime bhavantu pitaro loke mayā sṛṣṭāḥ sanātanāḥ
english: "These three, though formless, now bearing the form of the rice-ball, let them become the eternal fathers in the world, created by Me."

sanskrit: pitā pitāmahaś caiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ aham evātra vijñeyas triṣu piṇḍeṣu saṃsthitaḥ
english: "Father, grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather—I alone am to be known here, abiding within the three rice-balls."

sanskrit: nāsti matto 'dhikaḥ kaś cit ko vābhyarcyo mayā svayam ko vā mama pitā loke aham eva pitāmahaḥ
english: "There is none greater than Me; whom then should I Myself worship? Who is My father in the world? I alone am the grandsire."

sanskrit: pitāmahapitā caiva aham evātra kāraṇam ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ devadevo vṛṣākapiḥ
english: "And the father of the grandsire—I alone am the cause herein." Having spoken this word, the God of gods, Vṛṣākapi,—

sanskrit: varāhaparvate vipra dattvā piṇḍān savistarān ātmānaṃ pūjayitvaiva tatraivādarśanaṃ gataḥ
english: on the Boar Mountain, O brāhmaṇa, having offered the rice-balls in full ceremony, and having worshiped His own Self alone, vanished from sight there itself.

sanskrit: etadarthaṃ śubhamate pitaraḥ piṇḍasaṃjñitāḥ labhante satataṃ pūjāṃ vṛṣākapivaco yathā
english: For this reason, O fair-minded one, the fathers, called by the name of the rice-ball, ever receive worship, according to the word of Vṛṣākapi.

sanskrit: ye yajanti pitṝn devān gurūṃś caivātithīṃs tathā gāś caiva dvijamukhyāṃś ca pṛthivīṃ mātaraṃ tathā karmaṇā manasā vācā viṣṇum eva yajanti te
english: Those who worship the fathers, the gods, the teachers, and likewise guests, and the cows, and the foremost of the twice-born, and the earth their mother—by deed, by thought, by word, they worship Viṣṇu alone.

sanskrit: antargataḥ sa bhagavān sarvasattvaśarīragaḥ samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu īśvaraḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ mahān mahātmā sarvātmā nārāyaṇa iti śrutaḥ
english: That blessed Lord dwells within, abiding in the bodies of all beings, the same in all creatures, the Master over pleasure and pain, the great, the great-souled, the Self of all, who is heard of as Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śrutvaitan nārado vākyaṃ naranārāyaṇeritam atyantabhaktimān deve ekāntitvam upeyivān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this speech uttered by Nara and Nārāyaṇa, Nārada, supremely devoted to the God, attained to single-minded devotion.

sanskrit: proṣya varṣasahasraṃ tu naranārāyaṇāśrame śrutvā bhagavadākhyānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca harim avyayam himavantaṃ jagāmāśu yatrāsya svaka āśramaḥ
english: Having dwelt a thousand years in the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, having heard the tale of the Lord and beheld the imperishable Hari, he swiftly went to the Himālaya, where his own hermitage lay.

sanskrit: tāv api khyātatapasau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī tasminn evāśrame ramye tepatus tapa uttamam
english: And those two seers, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, renowned for their austerity, in that same lovely hermitage practiced the highest austerity.

sanskrit: tvam apy amitavikrāntaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ kulodvahaḥ pāvitātmādya saṃvṛttaḥ śrutvemām āditaḥ kathām
english: You too, of measureless valor, upholder of the line of the Pāṇḍavas, have this day become purified of soul, having heard this tale from its beginning.

sanskrit: naiva tasya paro loko nāyaṃ pārthivasattama karmaṇā manasā vācā yo dviṣyād viṣṇum avyayam
english: Neither the world beyond nor this world is his, O best of kings, who by deed, by thought, by word, should hate the imperishable Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: majjanti pitaras tasya narake śāśvatīḥ samāḥ yo dviṣyād vibudhaśreṣṭhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim
english: The fathers of that man sink in hell for everlasting years, who should hate the foremost of the wise, the God Nārāyaṇa, Hari.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāma bhaved dveṣya ātmā lokasya kasya cit ātmā hi puruṣavyāghra jñeyo viṣṇur iti sthitiḥ
english: How indeed could the Self of anyone in the world be an object of hatred? For the Self, O tiger among men, is to be known as Viṣṇu—such is the settled truth.

sanskrit: ya eṣa gurur asmākam ṛṣir gandhavatīsutaḥ tenaitat kathitaṃ tāta māhātmyaṃ paramātmanaḥ tasmāc chrutaṃ mayā cedaṃ kathitaṃ ca tavānagha
english: He who is our teacher, the seer, the son of Gandhavatī—by him was this greatness of the Supreme Self told, my child; and so it was heard by me and told to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ vyāsaṃ viddhi nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum ko hy anyaḥ puruṣavyāghra mahābhāratakṛd bhavet dharmān nānāvidhāṃś caiva ko brūyāt tam ṛte prabhum
english: Know Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa to be the Lord Nārāyaṇa; for who else, O tiger among men, could be the maker of the Mahābhārata? And who, save that Lord, could declare the manifold ordinances of dharma?

sanskrit: vartatāṃ te mahāyajño yathā saṃkalpitas tvayā saṃkalpitāśvamedhas tvaṃ śrutadharmaś ca tattvataḥ
english: Let your great sacrifice proceed as you have resolved upon it; you have vowed the horse-sacrifice and have truly learned the law.

sanskrit: etat tu mahad ākhyānaṃ śrutvā pārikṣito nṛpaḥ tato yajñasamāptyarthaṃ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ samārabhat
english: And the king, the son of Parīkṣit, having heard this great narrative, then set about all the rites for the completion of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇīyam ākhyānam etat te kathitaṃ mayā nāradena purā rājan gurave me niveditam ṛṣīṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca śṛṇvatoḥ kṛṣṇabhīṣmayoḥ
english: This narrative of Nārāyaṇa I have told you, O king, which was declared of old by Nārada to my teacher, while the seers and the Pāṇḍavas listened, and Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma too.
